topStories.headline: Prop G Puts Sunset Dunes Back on the Ballot — For the Third Time in Four Years
topStories.dek: San Francisco voters decide November 3 whether to reopen the Upper Great Highway to weekday car traffic, with the Sunset neighborhood once again at the center of the fight.
topStories.body:
For the third time in four years, San Franciscans will vote on the future of the two-mile oceanfront stretch that is now Sunset Dunes Park. Proposition G, on the November 3 ballot, would reopen the Upper Great Highway to private vehicles on weekdays while preserving portions of the existing park. A no vote would keep the road closed to cars at all times, as it has been since voters approved Prop K in November 2024 by a 55-to-45 margin and the city converted the roadway into Sunset Dunes in 2025.

The park has logged more than 1.7 million visits since opening in April 2025, according to San Francisco Recreation and Parks, ranking it the city's third-most popular park. Opponents of Prop G — including Senator Scott Wiener and five city supervisors — note that roughly 60 percent of those visits occur on weekdays, exactly the hours the measure would hand back to cars. They argue that passing Prop G would force the removal of park amenities already installed along the promenade.

Proponents counter that the full highway closure has pushed traffic into Sunset residential streets and worsened injury rates in the neighborhood. They frame the measure as a return to the weekend-only closure arrangement that held from 2021 to 2024. The San Francisco Controller's Office estimates reopening the road would cost $9.8 million upfront and as much as $1.9 million each year to maintain.

Prop G was placed on the ballot after organizers gathered roughly 10,600 signatures — about two percent of registered voters — certified by the Department of Elections on July 23, 2026. The SF Chronicle editorial board, which backed Prop K in 2024, recommended a no vote this cycle. SPUR also recommended voting no. Polls open November 3.

topStories.headline: Great Hauntway Fills Sunset Dunes With Costumes and Candy for Sixth Year Running
topStories.dek: Last Sunday's free Halloween festival on the oceanfront promenade drew families from across the city, cementing the park's role as a neighborhood anchor even as voters prepare to decide its future.
topStories.body:
The sixth annual Great Hauntway took over Sunset Dunes on Sunday, October 25, filling the promenade between Judah and Taraval streets with trick-or-treating, bounce houses, live performers, and music from 1 to 4 p.m. The event — presented by Friends of Sunset Dunes in partnership with San Francisco Recreation and Parks — featured more than a mile of candy stations along the upper Great Highway promenade, plus pumpkin decorating and big bubbles for younger children. Organizers describe it as the city's largest free Halloween event.

San Francisco Recreation and Parks ran a special edition of the Golden Gate Shuttle for Hauntway attendees, connecting the Judah Street entrance at Lower Great Highway to the Blue Heron Lake Boathouse and Transverse Drive inside Golden Gate Park — a car-free route in from the east that also served as a quiet reminder of what is at stake in Tuesday's Prop G vote.

The Shipwreck Cove playground, which opened at Sunset Dunes in September 2026, drew families on the day as well. Friends of Sunset Dunes continues its free programming on the promenade through the fall, with the 2nd Sunday Serenades on November 8 and a Zumba session on November 14 both on the calendar.

moreNews.headline: Profile: The Story Behind Irving Street's Texas-Chinese BBQ Joint, Smokin D's
moreNews.body: The Sunset Beacon published a feature on Smokin D's BBQ on October 18, 2026, telling the story of the Outer Sunset restaurant at 2181 Irving St. that has built a loyal following since opening its brick-and-mortar in August 2024. Owner Daniel Ramirez, who grew up in Houston, started the business running pop-ups at Bay Area farmers markets before settling into the Irving Street corridor with his wife Lareina Chu, a Sunset native. The menu blends Texas-style smoked brisket, pulled pork, and spare ribs with Chinese-inspired bao buns, with bao available on weekends only. The restaurant is open Friday through Sunday.

moreNews.headline: District 4 Supervisor Race Goes to the November 3 General Election
moreNews.body: Incumbent Supervisor Alan Wong, who won a June 2026 special election to fill the seat vacated by recalled Supervisor Joel Engardio, must win again on November 3 to hold the position for a full four-year term. His opponent is Jeremy Greco, a school campus coordinator, according to Axios San Francisco's voter guide published October 13. District 4 covers the Outer Sunset and Parkside neighborhoods. The SF Chronicle editorial board endorsed Wong this week, noting the district has been deeply divided over the Great Highway and Sunset Dunes for the past two years.
